subject: health
topic: Ultra-processed food makes people eat more without noticing
angle: While a controlled trial shows ultra-processed diets cause an increase of about 500 calories a day and weight gain, other studies show that breakfast cereals may actually reduce mortality risk.
title: The Engineering of Appetite

hooks.text: Why do you eat more without feeling full?
You assume ultra-processed food is just a choice. The evidence shows it changes your intake.
Your ultra-processed diet may be increasing your calorie intake every day.
A bowl of cereal on a kitchen table.

reveal.headline: You eat more without noticing.
reveal.body: In a controlled trial, an ultra-processed diet caused an energy intake 508 kcal/day greater than an unprocessed diet. The evidence is mixed.,,

explain.headline: The data is contradictory.
explain.body: While ultra-processed foods are linked to a 15% higher risk of all-cause mortality, high consumption of breakfast cereals is linked to a lower mortality risk.

matters.headline: Design influences your appetite.
matters.body: That may be why ultra-processed foods lead to higher calorie intake in controlled settings. Your choices are influenced by how your food is engineered.

example.headline: A bowl of cereal.
example.body: You sit at the kitchen table in the morning. You pour the flakes into a bowl. You eat until the bowl is empty.

stat.label: extra energy intake from an ultra-processed diet in a controlled trial

claims.text: High consumption of breakfast cereals is linked to a lower mortality risk.
claims.quote: However, breakfast cereals were associated with a lower mortality risk (RR = 0. 85, 95% CI, 0. 79, 0. 92).

claims.text: Each 10% increase in ultra-processed food consumption in daily calorie intake is linked to a 15% higher risk of all-cause mortality.
claims.quote: each 10% increase in UPF consumption in daily calorie intake was associated with a 15% higher risk of all-cause mortality (OR = 1. 15; 95% CI: 1. 09, 1. 21; I2 = 0. 0%; p < 0. 001).

claims.text: In a trial of 20 weight-stable adults, an ultra-processed diet caused an energy intake that was 508 ± 106 kcal/day greater than an unprocessed diet.
claims.quote: Energy intake was greater during the ultra-processed diet (508 ± 106 kcal/day; p = 0. 0001), with increased consumption of carbohydrate (280 ± 54 kcal/day; p < 0. 0001) and fat (230 ± 53 kcal/day; p = 0. 0004), but not protein (-2 ± 12 kcal/day; p = 0. 85).

claims.text: Highest consumption of ultra-processed foods is linked to an increased risk of all-cause mortality in five studies.
claims.quote: highest UPF consumption was found to be associated with increased risk of all-cause mortality in five studies (risk ratio (RR) 1·25, 95 % CI 1·14, 1·37; P < 0·00001)

verdict: The evidence shows that ultra-processed foods cause higher calorie intake and weight gain in a controlled setting and are linked to increased mortality risks in observational studies.
caveat: The evidence for mortality risk comes from observational studies, while the evidence for increased calorie intake comes from a small trial of only 20 adults.
caption:
Ultra-processed foods may cause you to eat more calories without noticing.

The evidence for mortality is mixed as breakfast cereals are linked to lower risk.

Does your food choice feel like your own?
